why: Headnote holding that, on a succession opening in 1948, the daughter is excluded by a son, applying the pre-reform law; headnote confidence is capped.
Succession to a female Hindu's property, not coparcenary rights of daughters.

why: Historical account of women's reforms in a marriage-equality case, not coparcenary rights.

span: whether it is permissible for the employer to withhold the payment of gratuity of the employee even after his superannuation
why: Gratuity and continuation of inquiry after superannuation; dismissal follows an inquiry and no dismissal without inquiry is considered.

span: the State would still be empowered to dismiss an employee from service based on the conviction in the criminal case
why: Court notes dismissal on conviction as a consequence of waiting for criminal proceedings; it does not hold that dismissal without any departmental inquiry is permissible.

span: removal and dismissal from service stand on the same footing and both terminate the relationship of employer/ employee
why: Difference between removal and dismissal, not whether an inquiry is required.

span: When a departmental enquiry is conducted against the government servant it cannot be treated as a casual exercise.
why: Quoted statement on fairness within an inquiry, which is a different condition from dispensing with the inquiry.

span: A Gramin Dak Sewak is not an “employee” under the 1972 Act.
the employee was dismissed from service after holding departmental enquiry
why: The appellant's contention that its case differs because an enquiry was held; it is a party submission and the court's view follows.

span: Article 311 is confined to the cases wherein an inquiry has been commenced against an employee
why: Court explains the scope of Articles 309 and 311 in a compulsory-retirement challenge; it does not itself permit or forbid dismissal without an inquiry.

span: An employee is entitled to subsistence allowance during an inquiry pending against him or her
why: Subsistence allowance during an inquiry, a different condition.

span: The legal heirs on record can definitely file a civil suit for declaration
why: Remedy against a dismissal order for legal heirs; whether an inquiry is mandatory is not decided here.

span: the inquiry was conducted ex-parte and the copy of the Inquiry Report holding the charges as proved
why: Facts of an ex-parte inquiry; an inquiry was held, so it is not a dismissal without an inquiry.
